editorial:
Imagine living in France during World War II, where the rules are strict but people are just trying to survive. You meet Marie, a mother of two who isn't your typical housewife. She runs a secret business doing illegal abortions to make money and lets a local prostitute stay in her spare room. Her husband comes home from the war with an injury, but she barely cares about him. She is focused on her own money, her own power, and a spicy affair with a young lover. It feels like a slow burn that looks at how some people actually thrive when the world is falling apart around them.

What really works here is the acting; you can feel Marie's coldness and her drive to stay in control. The pace is steady, though some might find it a bit slow since it focuses more on conversations than big action. It is a great pick if you enjoy character studies about people who play by their own rules.
endingExplained: Everything falls apart when the police finally catch up to Marie. Her secret life and illegal medical work lead to her being arrested. The movie ends with her facing the consequences of her choices. You see a shift from her being the one in control to being totally powerless. It wraps up by showing that no matter how much money she made or how much she ignored her husband, the law eventually caught up with her.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves stories about strong women and secret lives in old Europe.
similarMovies: Jeanne Dielman, 23 quai du Commerce, 1080 Bruxelles
